topics.topic: When and how the single-home guarantee becomes enforceable and verifiable
questions: When does the single-home guarantee begin, and what observable condition proves that legacy instances and existing service stores no longer retain prohibited copies?
When does the single-home promise become effective, and may production Registry launch while another service still keeps a living customer record or copied values?
What action or acceptance condition establishes this promise, and what observable failure occurs if a consumer still stores a customer record or copied value?

quotes:
Registry is the one home of a customer's personal data: no other service keeps
a customer record or a copy of its values, except as fixed in a document it
issued (R0-80).

Legacy instances — the v1 Registries running before production: the one
on the VPS, inside Client Portal's network, and the local one. They hold real
personal data, are administered by the owner and stand outside this
document's guarantees. The VPS one is the migration's only source; each is
retired once the migration is done (R0-79).

Removing the stores and
copies the services keep today is each service's own change.
judgement.divergence: One implementer permits production launch while legacy instances and consumer services retain living copies, treating their later retirement or remediation as external work; another blocks acceptance or launch until those copies are removed. The owner and services observe whether multiple living stores coexist after the single-home promise is declared effective.
judgement.why: The texts assert the single-home condition and acknowledge prohibited copies but do not name when the guarantee takes effect or the acceptance failure that enforces it.
judgement.failure: the quoted passage of a consequential gap is not found verbatim in the texts

topics.topic: Whether PresuPro may receive the customer's ordinary name
questions: May PresuPro receive the customer's name, or is name contact data restricted to the owner?
May PresuPro receive the Customer's ordinary `name`, or only the fiscal/legal name and non-contact billing fields?
May PresuPro receive the customer's name when issuing a document, or is the name contact data restricted to the owner?

quotes:
Name, phone, e-mail and language are
all the customer's contact data: personal data, readable by staff only (R0-09),
and erasable as a whole.

The customer's contact data reaches the owner alone; its billing data
reaches the owner and a service whose token allows reading it (R0-80).
the customer named by `customer_ref`: name, kind, tax id, legal name
judgement.why: The ordinary name is defined as contact data confined to the owner, yet the PresuPro billing-data action returns that name.

topics.topic: Whether agent projections must exclude actual or indirectly accessible personal values
questions: Is the guarantee about actual personal values reaching the agent, or only about fields Registry formally classifies as personal_data?
Is the guarantee merely that fields classified by Registry as `personal_data` are excluded, or must Registry prevent personal values embedded in room names and pointer fields from reaching the agent?
Can a pointer exposed to an agent resolve to or authorize retrieval of an issued document containing personal data, and which component prevents that disclosure?

quotes: sees each through a minimal projection without personal values (R0-43),
the minimal projection of that project: its id, status, rooms and artifact pointers — no display name (R0-68), address, customer or other personal value

Registry does not inspect these values:
the rule binds their writers and is not a check of Registry, and a value that
breaks it is not refused and does reach the agent.
judgement.why: The projection is promised to contain no personal values while another passage expressly permits personal values embedded by writers to reach the agent.

topics.topic: Which customer data and project links survive customer erasure
questions: When a Customer is erased, are tax id, legal name, kind, restriction state and relationship-end date also removed, or does any of them survive?
Does this erasure also remove kind, tax id, legal name, restriction state and relationship-ended state, or does it retain some of them?
After customer erasure, do projects retain `customer_ref`, or must that identifying link be removed?

quotes:
Erasing a customer's contact data (R0-06) is the end of its record: the
Customer keeps its identity and the fact that it was erased, and projects keep
naming it. There is no action that deletes a Customer whole.
judgement.why: Only the Customer identity and erased fact survive in its record, while projects explicitly retain their references to that Customer.

topics.topic: Requirements for retained identifiers and pointers in anonymised projects
questions: What must happen if retained artifact-pointer fields contain or permit re-identification when the owner requests anonymisation?
What must be true of the retained project id and pointer fields before Registry may call the project anonymised?

judgement.why: The prior judgement already establishes the governance-recorded non-reidentification condition for retaining an anonymised project's identity and pointers.

precedent.topic: Conditions for retained artifact pointers and identifiers to be considered anonymised
quotes: A project's technical identity, status and artifact pointers are kept only where it is shown that they no longer allow re-identification and a justified purpose for keeping them is recorded; `validate` then answers `archived`. Otherwise the record is deleted whole, and `validate` answers `not_found`.
Narrowed by R0-60: the owner chooses between the two when erasing; the showing and the purpose are recorded in the governance.
precedent.why: Retention is permitted only after a governance-recorded showing that the retained identity and pointers no longer allow re-identification; otherwise the project is deleted whole.

topics.topic: Whether Client Portal's offline projection is covered by the issued-document exception
questions: Is Client Portal's offline projection an issued document covered by the stated exception, or is it a second distinct exception to the single-home rule?
Is Client Portal's offline projection an issued document covered by the Product statement's exception, or a separate exception that must be named there?

quotes:
Registry is the one home of a customer's personal data: no other service keeps
a customer record or a copy of its values, except as fixed in a document it
issued (R0-80).

Client
Portal's offline projection (R0-39) is Portal's publication to the customer:
it holds only what the customer's own cabinet shows, never a tax id, and is the
one kept copy this rule admits besides issued documents.
judgement.why: The Product statement names issued documents as the sole copy exception, while R0-80 names the Portal projection as an additional exception besides issued documents.

topics.topic: Whether and under what limits consumers may persist Registry snapshots or copied values
questions: May PresuPro, Cabinet or Client Portal persist any fields returned by `context`, `read a project` or `list projects`; if so, which fields and for what purpose?
Does a snapshot mean a transient response only, or may a consumer persist it; if persistence is forbidden, when must the copy disappear?
May another service store a copy of an object's identifying characteristics, or does the same Registry-only storage rule that applies to its address apply to them too?

quotes:
Every other service names a project by the Registry's identity
and reads that identity as a snapshot; none of them writes it back (V1-2).
the snapshot a consumer keeps: id, display name, status, address, `customer_ref` (never contact data), created and updated times (R0-04)

Other services
keep no customer record and no copy of these values; they read them by
`customer_ref` or project id when they use them.
judgement.why: The context action says consumers keep a snapshot containing copied Registry values, including the address, while R0-80 says other services keep no copy of those values.

topics.topic: Which personal values Client Portal may retain in its offline projection
questions: Exactly which Registry values may Client Portal persist in its offline projection, especially customer name, phone, e-mail, language, legal name and object address?
Which exact personal values may the Client Portal offline projection persist, particularly customer name, contact data, project display name and object address?

quotes:
Client
Portal's offline projection (R0-39) is Portal's publication to the customer:
it holds only what the customer's own cabinet shows, never a tax id, and is the
one kept copy this rule admits besides issued documents.

What the
projection holds and how old it may be is Portal's design, bounded by the
disclosure classes its token allows (R0-26).
judgement.why: The exact fields permitted in the persisted Portal projection are an output-contract and schema question owned by State 6, and the text expressly assigns the projection's contents to Portal's design.

topics.topic: Which projects may be selected for the one-time VPS import
questions: May the owner select any VPS projects at import time, or must production accept exactly the two named project ids?
Is the import restricted to exactly the two named project ids, may the owner choose either subset, or may the owner select any projects present in the VPS export?

quotes: import projects with their identity | owner, confirming, from the VPS instance: the projects the owner picks (R0-79)

The only source is the Registry on the VPS, imported once. The owner picks the
projects: today "Comunidad de Propietarios C/ del Progreso 140"
(`37241411-f235-4a32-bb31-9629d1079dd2`) and the project of Uliana Kolpacheva
(`c276a851-9b8a-44c7-bbf7-20e363b0ad5f`), under the ids Client Portal already
names.
judgement.divergence: One implementer accepts only the two named project ids; another lets the owner choose any subset or any projects from the VPS. The owner observes which selections the one-time import accepts, and production consumers observe which identities exist afterward.
judgement.why: The phrase “the projects the owner picks” permits an open selection, while “today” names two projects without saying whether they form a mandatory closed set.

topics.topic: Which service owns living tax IDs and legal names
questions: Is the R0-37 customer bullet superseded so that Registry is the sole living store of tax id and legal name?
Which service owns living tax ids and legal names?

quotes:
Narrowed by R0-25 (no operator reads the phone; only the owner reads contact
data) and R0-37 (the customer's kind joins the record; restriction of
processing joins erasure) and R0-60 (erasing an archived project is a second
exception to R0-03, so erasure is no longer the only one) and R0-80 (fiscal data
joins the record; PresuPro keeps none).

A customer's living personal data — name, contact data, tax id (NIF/NIE/CIF),
legal name — and the object's address are held only by Registry.

PresuPro keeps a tax
id or legal name only inside the documents it issued.
judgement.why: R0-80 explicitly supersedes the earlier fiscal-data placement: Registry owns living tax ids and legal names, while PresuPro may retain them only in issued documents.

topics.topic: Allowed unauthenticated requests for authentication bootstrap
questions: Which unauthenticated requests are allowed to establish the owner's authenticated session, and what do they return or refuse?

topics.topic: Behavior when a requested project becomes ungrantable before an answer is applied
questions: If the selected project is archived, erased, deleted, or otherwise ceases to be grantable before the answer is applied, is the answer refused, and does the pending request remain?

topics.topic: External AI provider and trust boundary for Registry-derived data
questions: Which external model provider, if any, receives the agent projection and other Registry-derived values, and what trust boundary applies to that transfer?

topics.topic: Meaning and concurrency guarantees of the session access version
questions: What does the access version version, when does it advance, and does it provide stale-change protection for grants, revocations, active-project changes and request answers?

topics.topic: Revision checking requirements for all Customer and Project mutations
questions: Must every mutation of a Project or Customer supply its expected revision, return the next revision, and refuse a stale revision?

topics.topic: Semantics of repeated customer lifecycle transitions
questions: Are repeated restrict, lift, end and resume commands idempotent, refused, or accepted as new changes with new revisions, dates and audit entries?

topics.topic: The event that makes a document issued and the handling of failed or cancelled issuance
questions: What observable event makes a draft an issued document entitled to retain fixed personal values, and what happens if issuance fails or is cancelled?

topics.topic: Whether service project-card responses include embedded Customer values
questions: Does a service's project-card response contain only the project's `customer_ref`, or does “project card” include the embedded Customer values shown on the owner's card?

topics.topic: Which actions must create audit entries
questions: Exactly which primary actions create audit entries, especially state-changing actions performed through Kernel?
